title: Or any boon you think equal: be great on the earth
theme: Death widens the offer: if Naciketas thinks any other boon equal, let him choose it, with wealth and long life; he may rule on the earth, and Death will give him a share of every desire.

words.role: main verb of the last clause

sandhi.rule: etat before t stays: etat tulyam, written together. tulyam before the consonant y becomes tulyaṃ, P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः).

sandhi.type: visarga before t; m before a vowel
sandhi.rule: naciketaḥ before t becomes naciketas, P. 8.3.34 (विसर्जनीयस्य सः). tvam keeps its m before the vowel of edhi.

samasa.meaning: the great earth; Śaṅkara glosses «महत्यां भूमौ»
one who enjoys his desires; Śaṅkara: «कामभागिनं कामार्हं»

morphology.note: Imperative 2nd sg. of as ‘to be’; Raṅgarāmānuja notes the form — «अस्तेः लोण्मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्».
Enclitic accusative of the 2nd person pronoun; Śaṅkara glosses «त्वां».

translation.literal: If you think [some] boon equal to this, choose [it], wealth and long life; on the great earth, Naciketas, be [king]; of desires I make you a partaker of desire.
translation.readable: If you think any boon equal to this, choose it, and wealth and long life with it. Be great on the wide earth, Naciketas; I will make you the enjoyer of every desire.

anvaya: नचिकेतः, यदि एतत् तुल्यम् [अन्यम्] वरम् मन्यसे, [तम्] वृणीष्व, वित्तम् चिरजीविकाम् च [वृणीष्व] । त्वम् महाभूमौ [राजा] एधि । त्वा कामानाम् कामभाजम् करोमि ।
syntax: A conditional (yadi manyase) with an imperative apodosis (vṛṇīṣva), whose objects are extended loosely (vittaṃ cirajīvikāṃ ca); then an imperative of ‘be’ with a locative of place; then a first-person promise with a double accusative (tvā … kāmabhājaṃ karomi) and a partitive genitive.

ambiguities.note: From as, ‘be [king] on the great earth’: Śaṅkara supplies «राजा», and Raṅgarāmānuja names the form. The letters also allow edh ‘grow, prosper’, but no commentator used here takes it so.

beginner: Death does not give up. If none of the gifts he listed is good enough, he says, then name any gift you think is equal to your question, and take wealth and long life with it. Rule over the wide earth. I will make you someone who enjoys every pleasure he could want. Śaṅkara points out why Death can promise this: as a god, what he wills comes true. The offer is now open-ended — anything at all, except the one thing the boy asked for. The test is becoming harder, because now the boy cannot say that the offer was too small.
analogy: Like being told ‘name your price’ — the moment when it becomes clear whether there is a price at all.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Any boon the boy thinks equal, together with wealth and long life; kingship on the great earth; and a share in every desire.

commentary.q: How can Death promise every desire?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Śaṅkara: «कामानां दिव्यानां मानुषाणां च त्वा त्वां कामभाजं कामभागिनं कामार्हं करोमि», for, as Death says of himself, «सत्यसङ्कल्पो ह्यहं देवः» — a god whose will comes true. ‘Be’ means be king: «महत्यां भूमौ राजा नचिकेतः त्वम् एधि भव».

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: Raṅgarāmānuja: edhi is the imperative, second person singular, of as — «अस्तेः लोण्मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्»; ‘king’ is to be supplied («राजेति शेषः»).

advaita.text: Death, a god whose resolves come true, offers the enjoyment of divine and human desires: «सत्यसङ्कल्पो ह्यहं देवः».

visistadvaita.text: He reads the verse plainly, explaining the forms (edhi: «अस्तेः लोण्मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्») and taking kāmabhāj as one who enjoys the objects of desire.

schools.disagreement: The verse is not disputed. Madhva’s bhāṣya on the passage 1.1.22–25 comments only on the ‘do not ask’ of 1.1.25.

contemporary.text: ‘Name anything you think is equal’ is the strongest form of temptation, because it removes the excuse that the offer was too small. What it tests is whether anything is, for us, beyond price. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: Is there anything you would not exchange for any amount of money?
reflect.deeper: What makes a question worth more than every answer to other questions?
reflect.practice: Notice, today, one moment when you settle for something easier than what you really wanted to ask for.
